label: original-phase input from 3rd token on (mid-sequence encoding)
explanation: Fires only while original tokens are being read: about 99.9% of activation mass is in the original phase, from step 2 onward, peaking at t=3-5 (fires on 65-75% of those steps). It is essentially silent at t=0, weak at t=1, almost never fires on the <DEL> step, and never fires during the copy phase. Within that window it fires on only about 60% of steps, and which ones depends on the token without a clean rule. The input c gives the largest activations (top examples are c around t=4, often after early v/k), and w, d, z, f are also elevated. A token that is repeating an earlier input fires far less often (6% vs 35%). (phase==0)&(t>=2) gets dev F1 0.75, recall 0.99, mass recall 0.99, precision 0.61. Adding first-occurrence or position limits did not improve F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: c, w, d, z; t=2: c, d, w, f; t=8: c, w, d, s) and the first original token (most: v, y, k, h, j, n; least: c, z, f, 0); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
